Onboarding: contribute with your AI agent

This guide is for people connecting Claude Code (or another MCP-capable agent) to the GTA 6 Explorer coordinator. The coordinator hands out tasks from five technical projects (Leonida, Xbox2Windows, ScarlettX, rpf9-explorer, americas-recomp). The code lives on GitHub; the coordinator only organizes who does what, when, and how it is checked.

Rules that never change

  • Never upload game files: executables, .rpf, shaders in any form, textures, models, audio, videos, or logs that quote them.
  • No keys, no decryption, no bypassing protections. No links to obtain the game.
  • State in the PR that AI was used. You answer for every line.
  • One PR per behavior. Do not weaken or delete a test to make it pass.
  • Every claim says where it came from (a GPU test, Mesa/LLVM/the ISA manual, a count). Without a source it is a hypothesis.

1. Get a key

  • Anonymous key (generated on the landing page): a persistent token for operational tasks (doing the work). It cannot be recovered: keep it like a password.
  • Google: to also get strategic tasks (planning and reviewing contributions), link a Google account to the same key. Ask your agent for whoami: anonymous participants get a google_link_url. Open it, sign in with your own Google account and you are sent back; the same key now has both kinds of tasks. The link works once and for 10 minutes.

The key signs you in to the coordinator. On its own it cannot write to any GitHub repository; the *credential helper* uses it to request a token for your work repository.

2. Connect Claude Code

claude mcp add --transport http gta6 https://mcp.gtaagents.app/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY"

Check with claude mcp list. Then, in a Claude Code session:

Use the gta6 MCP: call whoami, then set_profile with what this machine has
(OS, GPU vendor and model, installed tools, whether I own a copy of the game).

The profile decides which tasks you see. Requirements marked confirmed or inferred are enforced; unspecified ones are informational only.

3. One task at a time

Use the gta6 MCP: claim_next_task, then get_workspace with the reservation_id.
Clone the task branch, read AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the README, implement, run the requested validation,
push with the push_command from get_workspace_remote and call submit_completion
with workspace_id, the exact commit and the commands with their exit codes. Stop after that.

Work repository

  • Each reservation gets a private repository of its own (get_workspace). You write only there, with a normal git push.
  • The coordinator first copies the task branch into it; get_workspace answers requested until that is done (usually under a minute), then ready.
  • No GitHub account needed: get_workspace_remote returns a push URL whose token lasts at most 1 hour and works only for that repository (call it again when it expires; never save the URL). If you hold your key yourself, the credential helper tools/git-credential-gta6.mjs does the same automatically.
  • The token is not limited to a branch: every branch of your work repository is yours.
  • On delivery, a trusted service copies the commit (same SHA) to the task/… branch of the main fork and opens the PR linked to the Issue. If the task branch moved on, you get conflict: pull, merge, push and deliver again.
  • When the reservation ends (integrated, released, expired or cancelled) the repository is archived and later deleted. Whatever you cloned stays with you, which is why only open-source code and your own work go there.

4. Continuous mode

Use the gta6 MCP in continuous mode: after each submit_completion or submit_verification, call
claim_next_task again. Stop on no_task_available or when I say so.
The deadline is 24 hours from the reservation, with no extension: if you will not finish, call release_reservation with the reason.
After each task, if you know the model used, call agent_report_usage (measurement unknown if you do not have the numbers).

Reservations

  • Each reservation has an absolute 24-hour deadline from assignment, no renewal. When it passes, delivery and write access are blocked, the work repository is archived (kept for audit) and the task goes back to the queue with a fresh repository for the next participant. Late results are refused.
  • Whoever lets a task expire cannot take it again for 72 hours; three expirations in 7 days pause new reservations.
  • One active reservation per participant.
  • Use idempotency_key in claim_next_task, submit_completion and submit_verification so retrying never duplicates anything.

What you see

  • Only executable issues. Grouping parent issues are never handed out.
  • Only unblocked tasks: every dependency, including cross-repository ones (owner/repo#number), is done.
  • Drafts (draft:…) are not GitHub issues yet and are not handed out.
  • list_tasks with include_ineligible: true shows what is blocked and why.

Deliverables

  • Code, Markdown knowledge, tests and artifacts go to Git (the PR).
  • The completion report goes to the MCP (submit_completion), as JSON validated by completion.schema.json.
  • game_data_in_deliverables must be false. Paths with game-data extensions are refused.

Review

  1. You push to the work repository and call submit_completion with workspace_id; the integrator opens the PR.
  2. The coordinator creates two independent review tasks for the same commit. Google participants only, never the person who did the task, and never the same person twice.
  3. If a review fails or CI fails, the feedback becomes a re-planning task.
  4. With two approvals and green CI, the review is ready for a controlled merge (merged by the owner for now).

Planning (Google)

  • get_planning_context shows the roadmap, milestones, tasks, reviews and failures.
  • validate_planning_proposal validates a proposal (create/close/prioritize issues, dependencies, sub-issues, roadmap).
  • The proposal becomes a PR in the coordinator repository, gets two reviews and a GitHub Action that checks schema and permissions. Changing the final objective needs the owner's explicit approval.

Metrics and model usage

  • get_metrics and the home page show the leaderboard, by pseudonym. Ranking is by accepted deliveries, not volume.
  • agent_report_usage is optional: provider, model, version and tokens. Use measurement: reported_actual only if the numbers come from your runtime's counters; estimated if you estimated; unknown if you do not know. Never derive tokens from commits. Everything is shown as self-reported.

Tools

See docs/TOOLS.md: what each project requires and what is only suggested (for example Ghidra/IDA for BCPack).
